results.title: Fireworks unveils new products at Forge | Fireworks
highlights:
Fireworks unveils new products at Forge | Fireworks

NOV 03, 2026

# Fireworks unveils new products at Forge to help companies build specialized intelligence

At Forge, Fireworks unveiled new products to help companies build AI around their own expertise, data, and tasks, with faster inference, more model choice, new evaluation and serving capabilities, and greater enterprise control.

...

Our first annual conference opens today, bringing together leaders from AI-native startups, global enterprises, open-weight model labs, and more.

...

## Faster agents, with costs that fit the workload

AI agents often make multiple model calls to complete a single task. Each call adds to the time a customer or employee waits for a result, while running more agents simultaneously increases capacity pressure and cost. Teams need speed for time-sensitive work and more economical options for tasks that can wait.

Fireworks Ultra-fast, powered by NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, accelerates those time-sensitive workloads. It is now available in public preview, delivering speeds up to 1,500 tokens per second as demonstrated on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. That speed is especially valuable when delays accumulate across multiple steps: in a benchmarked 30-turn agent task, completion time fell from 1 minute to 8 seconds at ultra-fast.

For workloads where cost matters more than immediate completion, Background Mode gives teams a lower-cost runtime option at half price. This mode lowers cost per task for eligible work that can wait, such as data generation for evaluations and overnight research. Multi-day Prompt Caching lowers costs for repeated context, while higher rate limits support more concurrent agents.

Figure 1: Persistent agents pay for reprocessing context every time they resume after a pause, and background agents pay peak prices for work that could wait. Multi-day prompt caching and Background Mode reduce each of those costs.

Specialized models can also improve inference economics. Ember-1, a Fireworks model available on serverless and dedicated deployments, used about 40% fewer tokens while maintaining comparable quality to Kimi K3 in our evaluations.

...

Together, these capabilities help teams match inference performance and spending to the demands of each workload.

...

Today we launched Nexus Desktop, joining the Nexus CLI. Nexus now runs in the Codex app, Claude Desktop, and OpenCode, extending personalized model selection beyond coding to everyday knowledge work. New Pro plans start at $8 per month, and Teams plans start at $10 per seat per month. Enterprise plans add SSO, governance, shared budgets, and access controls.

Figure 4: Nexus Desktop connects the tools you use every day to Nexus with one switch per tool, so teams get model routing without touching a terminal.

As workloads grow, higher serverless rate limits, now generally available, let teams run more work concurrently without reserving dedicated capacity. Elastic Burst, also generally available, allows customers to exceed their normal usage ceiling when spare capacity is available, with no code or pricing changes.

...

Specialized Model Inference, now in public preview, extends a serverless approach to serving LoRA adapters, starting with GLM 5.3 Flash. Teams can evaluate a trained model and serve it through the Fireworks Serverless API with per-token pricing, no dedicated deployment to size, and no serving charge while it sits idle. They can keep a model in use while experimenting with the next version.

...

For enterprises that want to leverage their own infrastructure, Fireworks Sovereign, now in private preview, brings the company’s inference engine to customers’ cloud, neocloud, or data centers. It combines technology that can double the tokens per GPU dollar, or more, with expert management that lowers total cost of ownership, helping customers run open models within their chosen infrastructure.

Inference and training run inside the customer’s environment, under the security and change-control policies it already enforces. Regulated enterprises can meet data residency and model access requirements on infrastructure they govern, and AI capacity stays in the jurisdictions they choose. Because customers own the infrastructure and pick the models, a provider’s price change or model retirement can’t set their roadmap. Fireworks already manages over 25,000 GPUs in customer environments.

results.title: Fireworks expands European capacity With NVIDIA | Fireworks
highlights:
Fireworks expands European capacity With NVIDIA | Fireworks

NOV 03, 2026

# Fireworks expands European capacity with NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell platforms

At its inaugural Fireworks Forge conference, the company introduces Ultrafast for interactive applications, new cost efficiencies for long-running agents, and higher rate limits.

Fireworks, the platform for specialized intelligence, today announced an expanded collaboration with NVIDIA. Fireworks will expand its capacity in Europe with NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell Platforms. The planned expansion will also leverage the NVIDIA DSX AI factory platform and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking for leading performance and throughput per watt. At Fireworks Forge, its inaugural user conference, the company also introduced new capabilities spanning enterprise inference workloads: an Ultrafast inference preview for interactive applications that need immediate responses, multi-day prompt caching and background mode for long-running agents, and higher rate limits to support growing demand.

...

This NVIDIA accelerated computing footprint will support deployments across Europe beginning in 2027. The added capacity will help Fireworks meet growing regional demand for open and specialized models as enterprises move more production AI onto the platform. The expansion builds on Fireworks’ work with NVIDIA to optimize inference for enterprise workloads, connecting accelerated computing with the software and model expertise companies need to run their own specialized intelligence.

...

- Fireworks helps customers accelerate latency-sensitive workloads with Fireworks Ultrafast, now in public preview on the NVIDIA Blackwell Platform. Leveraging NVIDIA’s full-stack accelerated computing platform with over 1000 co-designed domain-specific libraries, AI models, and tools such as CUDA-X, Nemotron, and Nsight, Ultrafast combines faster model computation with efficient communication across GPUs to support responsive, real-time AI applications, achieving inference speeds exceeding 1,500 tokens per second.
- Multi-day prompt caching and background mode for long-running agents. Multi-day prompt caching reduces the cost of reusing large amounts of shared context across repeated model calls. Background mode dramatically lowers inference costs for work that can run without an immediate response. Together, these capabilities make it more economical for agents to keep working in the background over extended periods.
- Higher rate limits and sub-minute cold starts to support growing demand. Increased limits give customers more room to scale both interactive applications and background agent workloads.

# Muse Spark Open on Fireworks: Meta’s open weights model, available on US serverless

Muse Spark Open, an open weights model from Meta, is now available on Fireworks. It ranks first on Vals AI’s leaderboard for Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark and beats Claude Opus 5.5 on Rogo’s Big Finance Bench, running on US-only serverless with zero data retention.

Muse Spark Open, an open weights model from Meta, is available Day-0 on Fireworks. It’s an 816B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 42B parameters active per token and a 1M-token context window, built for long-horizon coding and agent work that has to stay coherent across very long sessions.

...

The cost difference is significant. results.title: Train Muse Glimmer for free: Our recipe for out-betting Jev
highlights:
OCT 20, 2026

# Train Muse Glimmer for free: Our recipe for out-betting Jev

One training pass, better predictions. See how we trained Muse Glimmer to outperform Jev on unseen Kalshi topics, then try the recipe with free SFT through November 30.

## TL;DR

- Muse Glimmer 30B is free to train with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) through November 30, kicking off our Free Weights Club.
- Tuned Muse Glimmer outperformed Jev by 11.2 percentage points in prediction accuracy on unseen topics, reaching 58.3% versus 47.1%. In a historical backtest, it also turned a hypothetical $1,000 into $1,071 after modeled trading fees, while both Jev and base Glimmer lost money.
- Fireworks’ optimized System One serving stack delivered 2-3× faster median server processing than standard BF16 chat completions in a separate synthetic benchmark. Both used the same adapter and a single B200 GPU; precision and runtime differed.
- Try our experiment with the Kalshi cookbook. For your own projects, Managed Training runs the SFT job from your examples, while the Serverless Training API gives you control over the training loop.

...

First up: Muse Glimmer 30B, with SFT training free through November 30. It’s multimodal, offers strong performance for the cost, and makes a great starting point for personal agents.

We call the version we trained tuned Glimmer and the original model base Glimmer. Tuned Glimmer came out ahead of both comparison models on prediction accuracy. In a historical backtest, it turned a hypothetical $1,000 into $1,071 after modeled fees, while both comparison models lost money.

...

A confident prediction still needs a worthwhile price. If a bet pays $1 when it wins and the model estimates an 80% chance of winning, its expected payout is 80¢. Our rule required the purchase price plus modeled fees to be at least 5¢ below that estimate.

We gave each model $1,000 in hypothetical money to allocate across qualifying bets. Every model used the same rule and the same set of eligible historical quotes. An outcome had to have more than a 50% predicted chance of winning, and higher probabilities received larger allocations.

We used the last completed hourly bid/ask quote at or before two hours after each market opened. The models never saw those prices; we used them afterward to decide which bets qualified.

Tuned Glimmer’s allocation finished at $1,071 (+7.1%), compared with $950 for base Glimmer (−5.0%) and $919 for Jev (−8.1%), after modeled trading fees. We were glad to keep those last two losses hypothetical.

...

Muse Glimmer 30B is free to train with SFT through November 30, with no credit card required. Inference, including evaluation calls, is billed separately.

results.title: Paper Instruments trains a frontier-level model for knowledge work at ~98% lower cost
highlights:
OCT 28, 2026

# Paper Instruments trains a frontier-level model for knowledge work at ~98% lower inference cost

Built on Fireworks for professional analysis, writing, and presentations, Ultramarine 1 Flash outscored Fable 5 on Paper Instruments’ knowledge-work benchmark. Ultramarine is now available through Fireworks serverless inference.

...

Results

- Outscored Fable 5 at ~98% lower inference cost. Ultramarine scored 59.3 versus 57.8 at $0.13 versus $8.19 per task on Paper Instruments’ internal knowledge-work benchmark, giving the company a competitive offering on quality and price.
- A differentiated model for agent builders. Ultramarine gained 4.1 points on average over its base model across six knowledge-work benchmarks, giving Paper Instruments evidence to win over builders who might otherwise use the base model directly.
- Faster time to market. The team estimated that tuning GPU configurations itself would have delayed them by one to two weeks. Fireworks’ model-specific optimization helped Paper Instruments bring Ultramarine to market sooner.

...

On Paper Instruments’ internal PI Knowledge Work benchmark, Ultramarine 1 Flash scored 59.3 versus Claude Fable 5’s 57.8, at $0.13 versus $8.19 per task.

Benchmark results are reported by Paper Instruments. PI Knowledge Work is an internal evaluation. The Fable 5 comparison uses Fable 5’s maximum reasoning setting and each provider’s official API pricing; cost per task refers to inference, not model development.
